deep.reconstruction:
Context and caveat. This is a sheet of working diagrams from the 'Abelianization' bundle of notes (from 1982 on, roughly contemporary with Pursuing Stacks). Several key abbreviations cannot be decoded with certainty, notably 'surbm' and 'MU-fibré' (which replaces a crossed-out 'multibundle'). The reading below is a best guess.

(1) Basic pattern (top left). A square is drawn with rows alpha ->> beta <-' gamma and X ->> Y <-' Z, vertical maps xi and eta, and a dashed middle vertical beta --> Y. This is the standard situation where a map is factored as an epi-like map ('surbm') followed by a mono. Given the outer verticals, one asks for, or studies, the induced middle map.

(2) Zigzag (top right). The top row is a chain alpha_0 ->> alpha'_0 <-' alpha_1 -> alpha_2 -> ... -> alpha_{n-1} ->> alpha'_{n-1} <-' alpha_n, with a long map u drawn over it. The bottom row is the corresponding chain of X's, with a long map v drawn under it. The vertical maps are xi_i, eta_i and their primed versions. Grothendieck considers the systems (xi'_0, xi'_{n-1}) such that xi'_{n-1} u = v xi'_0. He says these form an 'MU-fibré' M_1, and that M is a functor of such 'systems' xi.

(3) Middle diagrams. For various sub-systems, the M-values are linked by restriction maps:
- M(xi_0,...,xi_n) -> M(xi'_0, xi_1, ..., xi'_n) -> M(xi'_0, eta_0, ..., eta_{n-1}, xi'_n) -> M(eta_0,...,eta_{n-1}) -> M(eta_0, eta_{n-1}).
- These maps are marked either 'surbm' or as cartesian squares ('cart').
- The comparisons are against M(xi_0) x M(xi'_n) and against products prod_{0<=i<=n-1} M(eta_i, xi_{i+1}, eta_{i+1}) and prod M(eta_i, eta_{i+1}).
- The aim seems to be to deduce that the composite restriction map, from the whole zigzag to its ends, is again 'surbm'. The method is: each map is a base change ('cart') or a composite of 'surbm' maps, and surbm is stable under composition and pullback.
This is a Kan-type or 'fibrancy' verification.

(4) Conclusion stated at the bottom. Consider a diagram I -> (semi-simplicial MU-fibred objects), i |-> X(i). For the integral ∫_I X(i) (a Grothendieck-construction / homotopy-colimit type total object) to stay within semi-simplicial MU-fibred objects, it suffices that:
- (a) Nerve(I) is aspherical (i.e. I is aspherical);
- (b) each X(i) sends the face operators ∂_i: Δ_{n-1} -> Δ_n to 'surbm' maps;
- (c) each transition map X(u), for u: i -> j, factors as g f with f 'surbm' and g mono.
The zigzags in (2) are exactly the simplices of the nerve of ∫_I X: chains i_0 -> ... -> i_n, with transition maps factored as in (1).

Plausible modern reading: 'surbm' = surjective submersion (or an abstract class of 'covering' epimorphisms), and an MU-fibred semi-simplicial object = a semi-simplicial object whose face maps belong to that class. If so, the page is a closure lemma: a Grothendieck-construction colimit over an aspherical index category of such objects stays in the class, provided the transition maps are (cover) ∘ (mono).
errors: The argument is only sketched in diagrams. The claim that the composite restriction map is 'surbm' rests on unstated stability properties of the class (composition, base change), on the 'cart' squares really being cartesian, and on the mono parts being compatible. None of this is verified on the page.

Condition (a), asphericity of I, plays no visible role in the diagram chase. It is presumably needed for a homotopy-type statement (∫_I X having the right homotopy type) rather than for the fibrancy property itself. As stated, the 'il suffit' mixes the two concerns.
Some diagrams are heavily overwritten (the red/crossed central part), so the exact intended maps there are uncertain.

ideas.what: Factorisation of transition maps as (surjective submersion-type epi) followed by mono, used to build the simplices of a total object over a zigzag
ideas.modern_name: (cover, mono) factorisation system; orthogonal factorisation used in Reedy/fibrancy arguments

ideas.what: Semi-simplicial objects whose face maps are 'surbm' (covering-type maps), with restriction maps to sub-systems being surbm or cartesian
ideas.modern_name: Kan / fibrant semi-simplicial objects in a category with covers; Lie n-groupoids à la Henriques/Zhu (horn maps surjective submersions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Henriques (2008), Zhu (2009), Wolfson, Rosenberg–Kapranov style 'categories with covers'

ideas.what: Closure of the class under the integral ∫_I X(i) over an aspherical index category, given conditions (a)-(c)
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck construction / homotopy colimit (Thomason's theorem) for diagrams of fibrant semi-simplicial objects
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thomason (1979) for hocolim = Grothendieck construction; asphericity: Grothendieck, Pursuing Stacks
ideas.where_published: Asphericity and integrals over categories pervade Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs; this specific lemma is not known to be there.

missed.claim: A sufficient-condition lemma: an integral ∫_I X(i) of semi-simplicial 'MU-fibrés' remains in that class if I is aspherical, the face maps are 'surbm', and the transitions factor as surbm∘mono. It is stated but proved only by sketched diagram chases. If 'surbm' means surjective submersion, this anticipates the closure properties of Kan simplicial manifolds / Lie ∞-groupoids under homotopy colimits, which received systematic treatment much later.
missed.quote: Pour que ∫_I X(i) ne fasse pas sortir des MU-fibrés semi-simpliciaux, il suffit que a) Nerf(I) asphérique ... b) Chaque X(i) transforme op. bord ∂_i : Δ_{n-1} → Δ_n en surbmersions, c) ∀ u ∈ Fl(I) ... X(u) se factorise en gf, f surbm, g mono.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Colimit and Grothendieck-construction stability for semi-simplicial objects in categories with covers (higher Lie groupoids, differentiable stacks) is still handled ad hoc. A clean criterion of this type would be of interest. Whether Grothendieck meant differentiable submersions or an abstract class is unclear.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical sketch with ambiguous terminology ('MU-fibré', 'surbm'). It may foreshadow fibrancy conditions for semi-simplicial objects with covers, but it is too fragmentary and uncertain to count as a clear unrecorded result.
transcription_corrections: 'surbm' is Grothendieck's abbreviation, most likely 'surbmersion' (surjective submersion?). It is written out once as 'surbmersions' in condition b).
The crossed-out words before 'MU-fibré' read approximately 'forment [stricte] multibundle'. 'MU' presumably abbreviates 'multi(bundle)'.
The products are indexed 0 ≤ i ≤ n-1 (written below ∏) in both rows, not 0 ≤ i ≤ n.
Condition a) reads 'Nerf(I) asphérique, i.e. I asphérique' rather than 'ou'.
The circled label under the bottom-left arrow is 'surbm' with '(rien[?])' below; the reading is uncertain.
The bottom-right small diagram has vertical labels η_0 and η_1 and a crossed-out middle β/vertical.
